RANDOM STRATA · BETA

Random, with a structure.

These four palettes were supplied by Coonie after a Gemini-assisted experiment. Their intended 32×32 layout has sixteen 8×8 sections: one random grayscale section and fifteen 24° HSV hue sectors. Each colored section calls for eight fully saturated, full-value colors, then fourteen samples from each of four saturation/value quadrants.

The supplied RGB values are preserved exactly. “Beta” distinguishes their actual colors from the stricter distance rule in the original prompt. The generator implementation was not supplied, so the audits describe the outputs without assuming why the rule was missed.

Distances use CIEDE2000 in CIELAB D65/2°, with kL = kC = kH = 1, measured on the final 8-bit sRGB values. A palette's minimum is its closest pair, not its typical spacing or its image-mapping error.

Four trials, one 4,096-color palette

The 4,096 source entries contain 3,949 unique colors: 3,777 colored entries and 172 grays. The 147 repeated occurrences divide into 84 grays and 63 colored entries. The combined beta includes every original unique color, all 256 true sRGB grays, and 63 new colored samples.

The new samples are chosen by deterministic farthest-point CIEDE2000 selection from random candidates stratified over the same fifteen hue sectors and four S/V quadrants, plus vivid candidates. Every new colored sample is at least 4.669 ΔE00 from every other final color. Existing close pairs and the deliberately complete grayscale remain intact.

Try 1 occupies the upper left, Try 2 upper right, Try 3 lower left, and Try 4 lower right. Only repeated occurrences are replaced: missing gray levels occupy duplicate gray cells, and new colored samples occupy duplicate colored cells. Those filled cells are chosen for coverage and do not retain the original cell's hue-sector quota.

A generator that checks the actual constraints

The original specification cannot meet a global 2.5 ΔE00 minimum. An exhaustive enumeration of the 256 gray codes, partitioned into pairwise-conflicting groups, proves an upper bound of 29 selectable grays at that distance—below the requested 64. The vivid row also conflicts with the rule: for example, the 96–120° sector permits at most two colors under the same upper-bound test, rather than eight.

The corrected script is a single Python file using only the standard library. It checks proven capacity bounds first, validates hue sectors and quadrants after rounding to byte RGB, rejects exact duplicates globally, and checks every accepted color against all earlier colors. It performs a separate all-pairs audit before writing anything. Search has finite retry budgets; failure never silently lowers a threshold.

Download corrected Python generator ↓Tested example with explicit exceptions · GPL ↓Example audit · JSON ↓

This strict invocation reports the infeasible requirements and writes no palette:

python3 generate-random-strata.py palette.gpl --seed 42

This tested invocation keeps the requested layout, explicitly allows dense gray and vivid rows, and retains 2.5 ΔE00 for every other pair:

python3 generate-random-strata.py palette.gpl --seed 42 \
  --gray-distance 0 --vivid-distance 0.25

Those options affect only gray–gray and vivid–vivid comparisons. Vivid–gray, vivid–quadrant, gray–quadrant and quadrant–quadrant comparisons still require 2.5. The sample has 1,024 unique colors and zero violations of these configured rules. Its global minimum is about 0.158 ΔE00 because the grayscale exception is real and explicitly recorded.

Use .gpl, .txt, .hex, .json or .png for the output; PNG is 32×32 RGB without alpha. Every successful run also writes an audit JSON sidecar. Change --seed for another random run. --check-only checks capacity bounds; passing that preflight is not a guarantee that bounded search will succeed. More retries are available through --restarts and --attempts-per-slot.

The CIEDE2000 implementation passes all 34 reference cases bundled with Gamut Forge. The demonstrated output is also checked independently with the project's NumPy implementation.
